events.title: Elizabeth I Charters the East India Company
events.description: Queen Elizabeth I granted a royal charter to a group of London merchants. It gave them a monopoly on English trade with the East Indies.
events.significance: The company grew from a trading venture into a powerful commercial and political force. It came to rule large parts of South Asia and shaped the course of the British Empire.

events.title: Battle of Quebec
events.description: Continental Army forces under Richard Montgomery and Benedict Arnold attacked Quebec City in a snowstorm. British defenders repulsed them. Montgomery was killed.
events.significance: The failed assault ended American hopes of making Canada a fourteenth colony. It marked the close of the Revolutionary War's northern invasion.

events.title: Edison Publicly Demonstrates the Incandescent Light Bulb
events.description: Thomas Edison showed his practical electric light to the public at his Menlo Park laboratory in New Jersey.
events.significance: The demonstration was a step toward electric lighting in homes and cities. It helped launch the age of electric power.

events.title: Yeltsin Resigns and the Panama Canal Passes to Panama
events.description: Russian President Boris Yeltsin announced his resignation on New Year's Eve and named Vladimir Putin acting president. On the same day, the United States handed full control of the Panama Canal to Panama under the Torrijos–Carter Treaties.
events.significance: Yeltsin's departure began the Putin era in Russia. The canal handover ended nearly a century of American control over the waterway.
